\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{إنجاز} (injāz)}{إنجاز (injāz)}]{\ar{إنجاز} (injāz) — an achievement}

\label{lesson:AR-C415-injaz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a consequence, then the Arabic for an effect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{إنجاز}}
\textbf{\ar{إنجاز}} — \emph{injāz} — \textquotedblleft{}an achievement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{الجسر} \ar{الجديد} \ar{إنجازا} \ar{كبيرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna al-jisr al-jadīd injāzan kabīran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The new bridge was a great achievement.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{إنجاز}} (\emph{injāz}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-j-z}, \textquotedblleft{}to be accomplished, finished\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Injāz} is the Form IV verbal noun of \emph{anjaza}, to accomplish: an achievement.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{injāz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{injāz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna al-jisr al-jadīd injāzan kabīran.} — The new bridge was a great achievement.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a consequence, then the Arabic for an effect, then say \emph{injāz} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{إنجاز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An achievement\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تأثر} (taʾaththara)}{تأثر (taʾaththara)}]{\ar{تأثر} (taʾaththara) — to be affected}

\label{lesson:AR-C415-taaththara-affected}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an effect, then the Arabic for an achievement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تأثر}}
\textbf{\ar{تأثر}} — \emph{taʾaththara} — \textquotedblleft{}to be affected\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تأثر} \ar{الأطفال} \ar{بالفيلم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʾaththara al-aṭfāl bi-l-film.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children were moved by the film.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتأثر}, \emph{yataʾaththar}.

It takes \ar{بـ}: \ar{تأثر} \ar{بـ} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تأثر}} (\emph{taʾaththara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-th-r}, \textquotedblleft{}a trace, a track\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to take a trace from a thing: to be affected, to be moved.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾaththara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾaththara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾaththara al-aṭfāl bi-l-film.} — The children were moved by the film.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an effect, then the Arabic for an achievement, then say \emph{taʾaththara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تبين} (tabayyana)}{تبين (tabayyana)}]{\ar{تبين} (tabayyana) — to become clear}

\label{lesson:AR-C415-tabayyana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an achievement, then the Arabic for to be affected.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تبين}}
\textbf{\ar{تبين}} — \emph{tabayyana} — \textquotedblleft{}to become clear\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تبين} \ar{أن} \ar{الخبر} \ar{غير} \ar{صحيح}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tabayyana anna al-khabar ghayr ṣaḥīḥ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It became clear that the news was not true.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتبين}, \emph{yatabayyan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تبين}} (\emph{tabayyana}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-y-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to be apart; to become clear\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to become plain: to become clear, to turn out.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabayyana}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabayyana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabayyana anna al-khabar ghayr ṣaḥīḥ.} — It became clear that the news was not true.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an achievement, then the Arabic for to be affected, then say \emph{tabayyana} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تبين} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To become clear\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{توصل} (tawaṣṣala)}{توصل (tawaṣṣala)}]{\ar{توصل} (tawaṣṣala) — to arrive at}

\label{lesson:AR-C415-tawassala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to be affected, then the Arabic for to become clear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{توصل}}
\textbf{\ar{توصل}} — \emph{tawaṣṣala} — \textquotedblleft{}to arrive at\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{توصل} \ar{الباحثون} \ar{إلى} \ar{نتيجة} \ar{جديدة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tawaṣṣala al-bāḥithūn ilā natīja jadīda.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The researchers arrived at a new result.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتوصل}, \emph{yatawaṣṣal}.

It takes \ar{إلى}: \ar{توصل} \ar{إلى} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{توصل}} (\emph{tawaṣṣala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-ṣ-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to arrive, to join\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to work one's way to a thing: to arrive at, to reach.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tawaṣṣala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tawaṣṣala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tawaṣṣala al-bāḥithūn ilā natīja jadīda.} — The researchers arrived at a new result.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to be affected, then the Arabic for to become clear, then say \emph{tawaṣṣala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{توصل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To arrive at\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مستوى} (mustawā)}{مستوى (mustawā)}]{\ar{مستوى} (mustawā) — a level}

\label{lesson:AR-C415-mustawa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to become clear, then the Arabic for to arrive at.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مستوى}}
\textbf{\ar{مستوى}} — \emph{mustawā} — \textquotedblleft{}a level\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{مستوى} \ar{الطلاب} \ar{جيد} \ar{هذه} \ar{السنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mustawā aṭ-ṭullāb jayyid hādhihi as-sana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The students' level is good this year.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مستوى}} (\emph{mustawā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-w-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to be equal, level\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Mustawā} is a noun of place from Form VIII, a level place: a level, a standard.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mustawā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mustawā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mustawā aṭ-ṭullāb jayyid hādhihi as-sana.} — The students' level is good this year.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to become clear, then the Arabic for to arrive at, then say \emph{mustawā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مستوى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A level\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
